title: SupportMesh product overview
content: SupportMesh is an enterprise customer-service system. Built on large language models, it understands natural language, classifies intent automatically and routes each request to the right specialist agent. It supports multi-turn conversation memory, so it remembers what the customer said earlier and keeps the conversation coherent. SupportMesh also ships with monitoring and evaluation built in, tracking live agent performance, surfacing problems automatically and generating improvement suggestions.

title: Plans and pricing
content: SupportMesh offers three plans. Starter: $19 per month, 1,000 conversations, 1 agent, basic intent recognition. Professional: $99 per month, 10,000 conversations, 3 agents, advanced intent recognition and memory management. Enterprise: custom pricing, unlimited conversations, any number of agents, the full monitoring and evaluation suite, and dedicated technical support. Every plan includes a 7-day free trial with no feature restrictions.

title: API integration guide
content: Integrating the SupportMesh API takes three steps. First, register an account and generate an API key under Settings -> API Keys in the console. Second, call the chat endpoint: POST to /chat with a body containing message (the user's message), user_id (the user identifier) and conv_id (the conversation identifier). Third, handle the response: the JSON returns response (the reply), intent (the recognized intent), agent_type (which agent handled it) and related fields. Full API documentation lives at /docs.

title: Common integration questions
content: Q: How should I handle API timeouts? A: Set a 30-second timeout and retry once on failure. A circuit breaker inside the system prevents retries from cascading. Q: How do I implement multi-turn conversations? A: Pass the same conv_id on every request and the system manages the context for you. Q: Which languages are supported? A: English is the primary language; other languages are handled but may perform less well. Q: How do I load my own knowledge base? A: Import documents through /knowledge/add or /knowledge/upload; the system chunks and vectorizes them automatically.

title: Data security and privacy
content: SupportMesh takes data security seriously. All data in transit is TLS encrypted. Conversation data is stored in isolated namespaces so that no two customers share storage. Conversation memory is cleared automatically after 24 hours by default, and Enterprise customers can define their own retention policy. Customer data is never used to train models. Self-hosted deployment is supported, keeping all data on the customer's own servers. The service is SOC 2 Type II certified.

title: Release notes v2.0
content: SupportMesh v2.0 highlights. New: 1. Three-way fused intent recognition (LLM + embedding + pattern), lifting accuracy to 92%. 2. Query rewriting and LLM reranking, lifting retrieval recall by 40%. 3. A three-tier memory architecture (working memory + episodic memory + user profile) with automatic compression. 4. Closed-loop monitoring feedback that adjusts agent routing weights dynamically. 5. An LLM-as-Judge evaluation framework that runs end to end with one call. Improved: the Docker image shrank from 3.5GB to 500MB. Fixed: an encoding crash caused by Unicode surrogate characters.
